title: Speculative decode proxy with kernel budgeting and temporal confidence smoothing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our existing speculative decode routing routes by model-only scores and separate kernel schedulers. This causes suboptimal kernel dispatch (mis-sized kernels, wasted warmups) and noisy acceptance signals when kernel startup or micro-batching jitter occurs. As a result, latency and token cost regressions surface on tail traffic and mixed workloads.

Goal: Implement a lightweight speculative-decode proxy (a routing shim inside the runtime) that: (1) integrates kernel budgeting (per-model/kernel short-term capacity tokens) into routing decisions; (2) applies temporal confidence smoothing on acceptance signals (EWMA with tunable window) to reduce flip-flopping; (3) exposes per-request fallback throttles when acceptance is uncertain; (4) ships with telemetry and can be A/B rolled for safety.

Non-goals: This ticket does not rework long-term model selection algorithms, replace global autoscaler, or change quantization internals. It is a targeted runtime shim for per-request routing and quick fallback behavior.

Design summary: The proxy lives between prefill probe and decode scheduler. For each incoming request the proxy computes a combined routing score = model_score * kernel_budget_factor * confidence_smoothed. Kernel_budget_factor is derived from a token-bucket: each kernel variant gets refill rate and burst sized based on observed throughput and startup cost. Confidence_smoothed is an EWMA of recent acceptance outcomes for the same (model,kernel) pair with decay configurable per-cycle-length. If combined score exceeds acceptance_threshold -> route to optimistic fast-path (speculative decode); otherwise route to conservative decode. On borderline requests, proxy attaches a fallback token that instructs decoder to checkpoint the KV cache and accept a fast fallback if the optimistic path stalls beyond timebox_ms.

Key parameters (configurable at runtime): acceptance_threshold, ewma_alpha (0-1), kernel_refill_rps, kernel_burst_tokens, timebox_ms, fallback_throttle_pct. These are exposed via console feature flags and can be changed per-customer tier.

Why kernel budgeting: Kernels with high startup cost (small batch optimized kernels) should be protected from being saturated by speculative probes. Budgeting prevents the router from over-committing a kernel variant during transient spikes.

Why temporal smoothing: Acceptance signals are noisy at low volume. Using EWMA prevents oscillation and reduces unnecessary fallbacks, improving tail latency and throughput stability.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy implemented inside runtime routing layer and compiled behind feature flag 'spec_proxy_v1'
Kernel budgeting token-bucket per kernel variant with metrics exported (tokens_available gauge, tokens_consumed counter)
Temporal smoothing implemented as EWMA with configurable alpha and window; smoothing exposed in telemetry
Router uses combined score to choose optimistic vs conservative flow; behavior matches spec in >= 95% of synthetic traces
Fallback tokens trigger safe KV checkpoint + bounded rollback on optimistic path within timebox_ms
E2E benchmarks show no >5% regression in p50 latency and measurable improvement in p95 tail for mixed workloads compared to baseline when enabled selectively
Unit and integration tests cover token-bucket edge cases, EWMA boundary behavior, and fallback code paths
Canary rollout plan validated with automated kill switch via console flag
telemetry: New dashboard: runtime / speculative-proxy / overview (acceptance_rate, combined_score_histogram, ewma_alpha, fallback_rate)
Alert: fallback_rate > 2% sustained over 5m in production triggers pager and auto-disable of spec_proxy_v1
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): unit tests + runtime-local smoke, target 2 engineers, 1 week
Stage 2 (internal canary): enable for internal team traffic only, monitor fallback_rate & p95 for 48 hours
Stage 3 (customer canary): enable for 5% of customer traffic with kill-switch and tight throttles for 72 hours
Stage 4 (gradual ramp): ramp to 50% over 14 days with adjustable kernel_budget params per-region
Stage 5 (full): enable per-customer opt-in in console and flip global default after 30 days of stable telemetry
tests: Unit: token-bucket refill/consume races, negative tokens behavior
Unit: EWMA computation tests for alpha edge cases (0,1,0.5)
Integration: synthetic mix workload (chatty short prompts + long streaming) comparing baseline vs spec_proxy
Integration: kernel exhaustion simulated by slow kernel startup latencies to validate fallback correctness
Load: 24h soak at 2x baseline QPS with randomized model mix to check stability of budgets and EWMA convergence
risks_mitigation: Risk: mis-tuned kernel budgets throttle legitimate traffic -> Mitigation: conservative default budgets and auto-backoff when fallback_rate spikes
Risk: state explosion from per-(model,kernel) EWMA -> Mitigation: cap cardinality via LRU eviction and coarse-grain buckets (family-level EWMA)
Risk: KV checkpoint overhead increases latency -> Mitigation: lightweight checkpoint (pointer-only) and benchmarked timebox to avoid decode stalls
Risk: complex interactions with autoscaler -> Mitigation: coordinate with autoscaler team and mark as dependency; fail-open behavior when autoscaler signals capacity shortfall
open_questions: Q1: Best default ewma_alpha and timebox_ms for multi-tenant mixed workloads? (experimentation required)
Q2: Should kernel_budget be global per-kernel or per-customer+kernal? (tradeoff: isolation vs complexity)
Q3: How to surface budget exhaustion to product (Console UX) without exposing raw kernel internals?
Q4: Interaction with existing speculative-prefill probe logic: replace or wrap? We currently plan to wrap initially.
